questions.q: What software does a fast food restaurant need?
questions.a: Most fast food operators start with a POS, then add tools for the areas that slow them down most. Common categories cover voice ordering for the drive-thru and phone, guest feedback and reviews, kitchen management, inventory and food cost, and labor scheduling. As you add locations, software helps you keep speed and consistency that SOPs alone can't hold across every store.

questions.q: How is AI used in fast food restaurants?
questions.a: AI takes drive-thru and phone orders, confirms items and catches errors before they reach the kitchen. In the back of house, it sequences tickets, tracks prep times and matches prep and ordering to forecasted demand. On the guest side, it replies to reviews across every channel and location and turns feedback into clear priorities for each store.

Yes, several voice AI platforms take drive-thru and phone orders automatically, often with built-in upselling and direct POS integration. Tools built for the drive-thru are tuned for speaker-box noise, and some support more than one language. They're mainly aimed at high-volume QSR brands that want to ease labor pressure during peak rushes.

questions.q: How can software help reduce food waste and food cost?
questions.a: Kitchen management tools forecast demand and tell your crew how much to prep and cook and when, which cuts over-production and stockouts. Waste trackers use computer vision to log what gets thrown away so teams can see the cost. Inventory and invoice tools track supplier prices and give you live food cost, so you order based on what actually sells.

questions.q: How do I choose software for a multi-location fast food brand?
questions.a: Begin with your biggest bottleneck, whether that's drive-thru speed, guest feedback, food cost or scheduling, and pick a tool built for that job. Check that it integrates with your POS and kitchen systems and that its pricing works at your number of locations. Many tools in this space use custom pricing, so ask for a quote based on your store count.

questions.q: How can a fast food brand keep up with guest reviews and messages?
questions.a: An AI agent can reply to reviews and guest messages on your behalf, quickly and in your brand voice, across every location. Momos does this with Alfie, which reads guest emotion from the review wording, visit history and preferences, then writes a personalized reply within minutes. It can also issue points, coupons and offers from your loyalty platform.
